claim: Insufficient insulin secretion to meet metabolic demand results in diabetes.
source: Insufficient insulin secretion to meet metabolic demand results in diabetes.
evidence: This is a well-established scientific fact in the field of diabetes research.

claim: The intracellular flux of Ca2+ into β-cells triggers insulin release.
source: The intracellular flux of Ca2+ into β-cells triggers insulin release.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-cell physiology.

claim: Genetics strongly influences variation in islet secretory responses.
source: Since genetics strongly influences variation in islet secretory responses, we surveyed islet Ca2+ dynamics in eight genetically diverse mouse strains.
evidence: This is supported by the study design and cited literature.

claim: High strain variation in Ca2+ response was found in 8 mM glucose condition.
source: We found high strain variation in response to four conditions: (1) 8 mM glucose; (2) 8 mM glucose plus amino acids; (3) 8 mM glucose, amino acids, plus 10 nM glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP); and (4) 2 mM glucose.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: High strain variation in Ca2+ response was found in 8 mM glucose plus amino acids condition.
source: We found high strain variation in response to four conditions: (1) 8 mM glucose; (2) 8 mM glucose plus amino acids; (3) 8 mM glucose, amino acids, plus 10 nM glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP); and (4) 2 mM glucose.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: High strain variation in Ca2+ response was found in 8 mM glucose, amino acids, plus 10 nM GIP condition.

source: These stimuli interrogate β-cell function, α- to β-cell signaling, and incretin responses.

claim: The stimuli used interrogate α- to β-cell signaling.
source: These stimuli interrogate β-cell function, α- to β-cell signaling, and incretin responses.
evidence: This is stated as the rationale for the experimental design.

claim: The stimuli used interrogate incretin responses.
source: These stimuli interrogate β-cell function, α- to β-cell signaling, and incretin responses.

source: We then correlated components of the Ca2+ waveforms to islet protein abundances in the same strains used for the Ca2+ measurements.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach used in the study.

claim: Human orthologues of correlated mouse proteins that are proximal to glycemic-associated SNPs in human GWAS were identified.
source: To focus on proteins relevant to human islet function, we identified human orthologues of correlated mouse proteins that are proximal to glycemic-associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms in human genome-wide association studies.
evidence: This describes the integration of mouse and human data.

claim: ABCC8 has previously been shown to regulate insulin secretion.
source: Several orthologues have previously been shown to regulate insulin secretion (e.g. ABCC8, PCSK1, and GCK), supporting our mouse-to-human integration as a discovery platform.
evidence: This is stated as validation of the approach based on known biology.

claim: PCSK1 has previously been shown to regulate insulin secretion.
source: Several orthologues have previously been shown to regulate insulin secretion (e.g. ABCC8, PCSK1, and GCK), supporting our mouse-to-human integration as a discovery platform.
evidence: This is stated as validation of the approach based on known biology.

claim: GCK has previously been shown to regulate insulin secretion.
source: Several orthologues have previously been shown to regulate insulin secretion (e.g. ABCC8, PCSK1, and GCK), supporting our mouse-to-human integration as a discovery platform.
evidence: This is stated as validation of the approach based on known biology.

claim: The majority of gene loci responsible for genetic variation in type 2 diabetes susceptibility affect the function of endocrine cells of pancreatic islets, primarily β-cells.
source: The majority of gene loci responsible for the genetic variation in type 2 diabetes (T2D) susceptibility affect the function of endocrine cells of pancreatic islets, primarily β-cells (Dimas et al., 2014; Wood et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Variation in β-cell mass and function places boundaries on their capacity to respond to acute and chronic demands for insulin.
source: Variation in β-cell mass and function places boundaries on their capacity to respond to acute and chronic demands for insulin, such as those of overnutrition and insulin resistance (Dimas et al., 2014; Wood et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Metabolic challenges are useful in genetic screens because they expose phenotypes that would otherwise remain silent.
source: Therefore, metabolic challenges are useful in genetic screens because they expose phenotypes that would otherwise remain silent.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the preceding discussion.

claim: The large collection of inbred mouse strains provides a wide repertoire of genetic and phenotypic diversity, comparable to that of the entire human population.
source: The large collection of inbred mouse strains provides us with a wide repertoire of genetic and phenotypic diversity, comparable to that of the entire human population (Clee and Attie, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: Most mouse studies have been confined to a small number of highly inbred strains.
source: Yet, most mouse studies have been confined to a small number of highly inbred strains (Clee and Attie, 2007; Kebede and Attie, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Gene deletions, nutritional interventions, and drug effects vary widely among mouse strains, as they do in humans.
source: It is becoming widely appreciated that gene deletions, nutritional interventions, and drug effects vary widely among mouse strains, as they do in humans (Clee and Attie, 2007; Sittig et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: In response to particular nutrient stimuli (e.g. glucose, amino acids), β-cells generate ATP and close ATP-dependent K+ channels (KATP), resulting in plasma membrane depolarization.
source: In response to particular nutrient stimuli (e.g. glucose, amino acids), the β-cells generate ATP and close ATP-dependent K+ channels (KATP), resulting in plasma membrane depolarization (Lewandowski et al., 2020; Foster et al., 2022; Merrins et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Plasma membrane depolarization leads to an oscillatory influx of Ca2+ ions, triggering insulin secretion.
source: This leads to an oscillatory influx of Ca2+ ions, triggering insulin secretion.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-cell physiology.

claim: The process of secreting insulin and re-compartmentalizing Ca2+ ions consumes ATP, and the drop in the ATP/ADP ratio reopens KATP channels, repolarizing the membrane, and closing membrane Ca2+ channels.
source: The process of secreting insulin and re-compartmentalizing Ca2+ ions consumes ATP, and the drop in the ATP/ADP ratio reopens KATP channels, repolarizing the membrane, and closing membrane Ca2+ channels.
evidence: This is established knowledge about β-cell physiology.

claim: Oscillations in metabolism, insulin secretion, and Ca2+ are intrinsically linked.
source: Consequently, oscillations in metabolism, insulin secretion, and Ca2+ are intrinsically linked (Merrins et al., 2022; Dahlgren et al., 2005; Krippeit-Drews et al., 2000; Marinelli et al., 2022b; Henquin, 2009), and the capacity to maintain functional Ca2+ handling has been suggested to be critical for islet compensation (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited references.

claim: The capacity to maintain functional Ca2+ handling has been suggested to be critical for islet compensation.
source: Consequently, oscillations in metabolism, insulin secretion, and Ca2+ are intrinsically linked (Merrins et al., 2022; Dahlgren et al., 2005; Krippeit-Drews et al., 2000; Marinelli et al., 2022b; Henquin, 2009), and the capacity to maintain functional Ca2+ handling has been suggested to be critical for islet compensation (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: The eight founder mouse strains used to generate the Collaborative Cross recombinant inbred mouse panel and the Diversity Outbred stock capture most of the genetic diversity of all inbred mouse strains.
source: In this study, we utilized the extraordinary genetic and phenotypic diversity represented in the eight founder mouse strains (which we subsequently refer to as 'founders') used to generate the Collaborative Cross (CC) recombinant inbred mouse panel and the Diversity Outbred (DO) stock (Threadgill et al., 2011; Svenson et al., 2012). These strains capture most of the genetic diversity of all inbred mouse strains (Threadgill et al., 2011; Svenson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: Studies of the eight founder mice have provided significant insight into genetic regulators of islet function.
source: While studies of these mice have provided significant insight into genetic regulators of islet function (Keller et al., 2019), determining the appropriate model system for evaluating genes of interest is often difficult, as most deletion models are made in only a small number of strains, primarily C57BL/6J or C57BL/6N.
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claim: Most deletion models are made in only a small number of strains, primarily C57BL/6J or C57BL/6N.
source: While studies of these mice have provided significant insight into genetic regulators of islet function (Keller et al., 2019), determining the appropriate model system for evaluating genes of interest is often difficult, as most deletion models are made in only a small number of strains, primarily C57BL/6J or C57BL/6N.
evidence: This is a statement about common practice in mouse genetics.

claim: The protein abundance from islets of the founder mouse strains is highly diverse.
source: Our prior proteomics studies showed that the protein abundance from islets of the founder mouse strains is also highly diverse, as is their insulin secretory response to different stimuli (Mitok et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference to prior work.

claim: The insulin secretory response to different stimuli is highly diverse among the founder mouse strains.
source: Our prior proteomics studies showed that the protein abundance from islets of the founder mouse strains is also highly diverse, as is their insulin secretory response to different stimuli (Mitok et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference to prior work.

claim: The human orthologues of many correlated proteins are encoded by genes with nearby SNPs linked to glycemic traits in GWAS.
source: The human orthologues of many of these proteins are encoded by genes with nearby single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) linked to glycemic traits (e.g. fasting blood glucose, see Table 2 for terms) in genome-wide association studies (GWAS).
evidence: This is a finding from the data integration analysis.

claim: Glucose metabolism, β-cell Ca2+ flux, and insulin secretion are pulsatile, and have been found to oscillate in both humans and mice.
source: Glucose metabolism, β-cell Ca2+ flux, and insulin secretion are pulsatile, and have been found to oscillate in both humans and mice (Merrins et al., 2022; Dahlgren et al., 2005; Nunemaker et al., 2006b; Kennedy et al., 2002; Lang et al., 1979).
evidence: This is supported by multiple cited references.

claim: Understanding the factors governing oscillation patterns can inform about the mechanisms that regulate insulin secretion.
source: Because they are interconnected, understanding the factors governing oscillation patterns can inform about the mechanisms that regulate insulin secretion (Lewandowski et al., 2020; Marinelli et al., 2022b; Colsoul et al., 2010; Corbin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: All mice were maintained on a Western-style diet high in fat and sucrose for 16 weeks prior to isolating their islets for Ca2+ imaging.
source: All mice were maintained on a Western-style diet (WD) high in fat and sucrose for 16 weeks prior to isolating their islets for Ca2+ imaging with Fura Red, a Ca2+-sensitive fluorescent dye (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Ca2+ dynamics were measured in response to 8 mM glucose.
source: We measured Ca2+ dynamics in response to four conditions: (1) 8 mM glucose (8G); (2) 8G + 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM leucine, and 1.25 mM alanine (8G/QLA); (3) 8G/QLA + 10 nM glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (8G/QLA/GIP); and (4) 2 mM glucose (2G) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Ca2+ dynamics were measured in response to 8G + 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM leucine, and 1.25 mM alanine.
source: We measured Ca2+ dynamics in response to four conditions: (1) 8 mM glucose (8G); (2) 8G + 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM leucine, and 1.25 mM alanine (8G/QLA); (3) 8G/QLA + 10 nM glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (8G/QLA/GIP); and (4) 2 mM glucose (2G) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Ca2+ dynamics were measured in response to 8G/QLA + 10 nM glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide.
source: We measured Ca2+ dynamics in response to four conditions: (1) 8 mM glucose (8G); (2) 8G + 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM leucine, and 1.25 mM alanine (8G/QLA); (3) 8G/QLA + 10 nM glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (8G/QLA/GIP); and (4) 2 mM glucose (2G) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Ca2+ dynamics were measured in response to 2 mM glucose.
source: We measured Ca2+ dynamics in response to four conditions: (1) 8 mM glucose (8G); (2) 8G + 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM leucine, and 1.25 mM alanine (8G/QLA); (3) 8G/QLA + 10 nM glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (8G/QLA/GIP); and (4) 2 mM glucose (2G) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There was a high degree of similarity between three of the five classical strains (A/J, B6, 129), which were dominated by slow oscillations in 8G and 8G/QLA/GIP.
source: There was a high degree of similarity between three of the five classical strains (A/J, B6, 129), which were dominated by slow oscillations (period 2–10 min) in 8G and 8G/QLA/GIP, and had relatively fewer islets reach plateau (continuous peak activity without oscillation) in 8G/QLA.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The classical strains (A/J, B6, 129) had relatively fewer islets reach plateau in 8G/QLA.
source: There was a high degree of similarity between three of the five classical strains (A/J, B6, 129), which were dominated by slow oscillations (period 2–10 min) in 8G and 8G/QLA/GIP, and had relatively fewer islets reach plateau (continuous peak activity without oscillation) in 8G/QLA.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The wild-derived strains (CAST, WSB, and PWK) closely matched one another, while differing from the classical strains.
source: Likewise, the wild-derived strains (CAST, WSB, and PWK) closely matched one another, while differing from the classical strains.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The wild-derived mouse islets were dominated by fast oscillations in 8G, resulting in plateaus for 8G/QLA and 8G/QLA/GIP.
source: The wild-derived mouse islets were dominated by fast oscillations (period <2 min) in 8G, resulting in plateaus for 8G/QLA and 8G/QLA/GIP.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Islets from NOD mice showed characteristics from both the wild-derived and classical strains.
source: Two strains stood out from the others. Islets from NOD mice showed characteristics from both the wild-derived and classical strains; slow oscillations in 8G and a sustained plateau in response to 8G/QLA and 8G/QLA/GIP with fast oscillations superimposed.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: NOD islets showed slow oscillations in 8G and a sustained plateau in response to 8G/QLA and 8G/QLA/GIP with fast oscillations superimposed.
source: Islets from NOD mice showed characteristics from both the wild-derived and classical strains; slow oscillations in 8G and a sustained plateau in response to 8G/QLA and 8G/QLA/GIP with fast oscillations superimposed.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: All NZO mice were diabetic (blood glucose >250 mg/dl).
source: The NZO mice also differed from the other classical strains, likely because they were all diabetic (blood glucose >250 mg/dl).
evidence: This is a measurement of blood glucose in the experimental animals.

claim: NZO islets were minimally responsive to 8G but did respond with a strong pulse in 8G/QLA and Ca2+ remained elevated in 8G/QLA/GIP.
source: Their islets were minimally responsive to 8G but did respond with a strong pulse in 8G/QLA and Ca2+ remained elevated in 8G/QLA/GIP.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Many of the strain differences seen in the male mice were maintained in the females.
source: Many of the strain differences seen in the male mice were maintained in the females (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All but one NZO female were diabetic.
source: Furthermore, the NZO females, of which all but one were diabetic, mirrored the behavior of the male islets.
evidence: This is a measurement of blood glucose in the experimental animals.

claim: The NOD females displayed a greater variation in their Ca2+ oscillations than the NOD males.
source: One interesting observation that emerged from the female islets is that the NOD females displayed a greater variation in their Ca2+ oscillations than the NOD males (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Some NOD female islets maintained slow oscillations throughout the various conditions.
source: Some of the islets maintained slow oscillations throughout the various conditions, while some demonstrated fast oscillations and plateaued like the wild-derived strains.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Some NOD female islets appeared strikingly similar to the islets from diabetic NZO mice, despite none of the NOD mice being diabetic.
source: Yet others appeared strikingly similar to the islets from diabetic NZO mice, despite none of the NOD mice being diabetic.
evidence: This is an observation from the data and blood glucose measurements.

claim: The one non-diabetic female NZO displayed oscillatory behavior comparable to that of the other classical strains, with clear, slow oscillations.
source: Finally, the one non-diabetic female NZO displayed oscillatory behavior comparable to that of the other classical strains, with clear, slow oscillations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Six parameters of the Ca2+ waveform were focused on: peak Ca2+, period, active duration, pulse duration, silent duration, and plateau fraction.
source: To elucidate strain differences in Ca2+ dynamics, we focused on six parameters of the Ca2+ waveform (Figure 2A): (1) peak Ca2+ (the maximum value of each oscillation); (2) period (the length of time between two peaks); (3) active duration (the length of time for each Ca2+ oscillation measured at half of the peak height, also known the oxidative 'secretory' phase, or 'MitoOx' [Merrins et al., 2022]); (4) pulse duration (active duration plus extra time for Ca2+ extrusion); (5) silent duration (the electrically silent 'triggering' phase, also known as 'MitoCat' (Merrins et al., 2022), which culminates in KATP closure and membrane depolarization); and (6) plateau fraction (the active duration divided by the period, or the fraction of time spent in the active 'secretory' phase).
evidence: This describes the analytical approach illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The transition from 8G to 8G/QLA resulted in an increased active duration, yielding a longer period and an increased plateau fraction in a representative B6 female islet.
source: A representative Ca2+ trace from a female B6 islet is illustrated in Figure 2A. The transition from 8G to 8G/QLA resulted in an increased active duration, yielding a longer period and an increased plateau fraction.
evidence: This is an observation from the example shown in Figure 2A.

claim: For an islet that plateaued at the peak, a plateau fraction of one, an active and pulse duration of 40 min, and a period of 0 min were computed.
source: For an islet that plateaued at the peak, as seen in 8G/QLA (Figure 2B), we computed a plateau fraction of one, an active and pulse duration of 40 min (the measurement time), and a period of 0 min.
evidence: This describes the analytical method for plateaued islets shown in Figure 2B.

claim: An islet that returned to baseline and ceased to oscillate was determined to have a plateau fraction, active duration, and pulse duration of zero, and a period of 40 min.
source: An islet that returned to baseline and ceased to oscillate, as seen in 2 mM glucose (Figure 2B), was determined to have a plateau fraction, active duration, and pulse duration of zero, and a period of 40 min.
evidence: This describes the analytical method for non-oscillating islets shown in Figure 2B.

claim: When KATP channels are pharmacologically closed with tolbutamide, the silent duration is shortened, resulting in increased frequency without a change in pulse shape.
source: Examples of pathways altering specific components of Ca2+ oscillations have previously been established (Figure 2D; Dahlgren et al., 2005; Marinelli et al., 2022b; Nunemaker et al., 2006b; Whitticar and Nunemaker, 2020; Koneshamoorthy et al., 2022). For example, when KATP channels are pharmacologically closed with tolbutamide, the silent duration is shortened, resulting in increased frequency without a change in pulse shape (upper panel).
evidence: This is supported by cited references and illustrated in Figure 2D.

claim: The addition of glucose leads to increased glucose metabolism and glucokinase activity.
source: The addition of glucose leads to increased glucose metabolism and glucokinase (GK) activity (Marinelli et al., 2022b).
evidence: This is supported by the cited reference and illustrated in Figure 2D.

claim: The rise in ATP from glucose metabolism inhibits KATP channels.
source: The resulting rise in ATP inhibits KATP channels (Lewandowski et al., 2020) and is used as a substrate for additional processes that affect Ca2+, such as SERCA pumps (Tengholm and Gylfe, 2017; Shuai et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by cited references and illustrated in Figure 2D.

claim: Glucose alters both the active and silent durations, resulting in a change in both frequency and shape of the Ca2+ oscillations.
source: Thus, glucose alters both the active and silent durations, resulting in a change in both frequency and shape of the Ca2+ oscillations (lower panel).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 2D and supported by the preceding discussion.

claim: WSB mice had significantly higher insulin secretion than 129 mice in each of the secretory conditions.
source: To determine whether average Ca2+ is predictive of insulin secretion, we performed ex vivo perifusion studies on islets from WSB and 129 male mice, two strains that showed similar average Ca2+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) but exhibited vastly different Ca2+ oscillations (Figure 1B). WSB mice had significantly higher insulin secretion in each of the secretory conditions (Figure 3A), suggesting another Ca2+ parameter better predicts insulin secretion.
evidence: This is a finding from the perifusion experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Average Ca2+ was not strongly correlated to insulin secretion.
source: Consistent with our observations from the perifusion data in the WSB and 129 islets, we found that average Ca2+ was not strongly correlated to insulin secretion.
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Active duration in 8G and silent durations in 8G/QLA were more highly correlated to insulin secretion than average Ca2+.
source: Other metrics, such as active duration in 8G, and the silent durations in 8G/QLA, were more highly correlated to insulin secretion.
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: The 1st component frequency in 8G from the spectral density analysis was highly correlated with decreased insulin secretion.
source: Meanwhile, the 1st component frequency in 8G from the spectral density analysis was highly correlated with decreased insulin secretion.
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Silent duration in 8G/QLA/GIP had the strongest correlations with plasma insulin.
source: These metrics were also the most highly correlated with multiple clinical measures in the founder mice, particularly plasma insulin (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Figure 4—figure supplement 3), for which silent duration in 8G/QLA/GIP had the strongest correlations.
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4B and supplements.

claim: Basal Ca2+ was relatively consistent among the strains, except NZO where it was highest in islets from male mice.
source: For example, basal Ca2+ (average Ca2+ in 2G, Figure 4C) was relatively consistent among the strains, except NZO where it was highest in islets from male mice.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: For the overall pulse duration, the NZO mice were the highest, followed by CAST and WSB.
source: For the overall pulse duration (Figure 4D), the NZO mice were once again the highest, followed by CAST and WSB.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: A noticeable sex effect was measured for the CAST mice, where male mice had a longer pulse duration than the female mice.
source: A noticeable sex effect was measured for the CAST mice, where male mice had a longer pulse duration than the female mice.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CAST has the highest 1st component frequency, followed by PWK and WSB.
source: The 1st component frequency (Figure 4E) is driven by the differences observed in the wild-derived strains, for which CAST has the highest frequency, followed by PWK and WSB.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The trend for a sex effect in the classic strains on the silent duration is absent in the NZO and wild-derived mice.
source: Finally, the trend for a sex effect in the classic strains on the silent duration (at 8G, 8G/QLA, and 8G/QLA/GIP) is absent in the NZO and wild-derived mice with the former having greater silent duration in males and the latter frequently having islets plateau in response to these stimuli.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Genetics has a profound influence on key parameters of islet Ca2+ oscillations.
source: Collectively, these data demonstrate that genetics has a profound influence on key parameters of islet Ca2+ oscillations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data presented.

claim: The previous survey of islet proteomics included both sexes for all strains, except NZO males, resulting in a quantitative measure of 4054 proteins.
source: Our previous survey of islet proteomics included both sexes for all strains, except NZO males, resulting in a quantitative measure of 4054 proteins (Mitok et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a description of the previously published proteomic data.

claim: Groups of proteins showed strong positive or negative correlation to a given Ca2+ parameter, yielding distinct correlation architecture.
source: Figure 5A illustrates a heatmap of the correlation between islet proteins and several parameters of Ca2+ oscillations. Unsupervised clustering was used to show that groups of proteins showed strong positive or negative correlation to a given Ca2+ parameter, yielding distinct correlation architecture.
evidence: This is an observation from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Proteins highly correlated to the 8G 1st component frequency tended to also be strongly anticorrelated to the silent duration conditions.
source: For example, proteins highly correlated to the 8G 1st component frequency tended to also be strongly anticorrelated to the silent duration conditions, which were very similar to one another.
evidence: This is an observation from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The active and pulse durations for 8G had nearly identical correlation structure.
source: The active and pulse durations for 8G had nearly identical correlation structure.
evidence: This is an observation from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The conditions with the fewest highly correlated proteins were the average Ca2+ measures for 8G, 8G/QLA, and 8G/QLA/GIP.
source: Additionally, the conditions with the fewest highly correlated proteins were the average Ca2+ measures for 8G, 8G/QLA, and 8G/QLA/GIP, and the structure for these was largely inverted from the active duration conditions.
evidence: This is an observation from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Among the 4054 islet proteins, 363 had high absolute correlation coefficients (r > |0.5|) to 3 or more of the parameters most strongly correlated to insulin secretion and plasma insulin.
source: Among the 4054 islet proteins, 363 had high absolute correlation coefficients (r > |0.5|) to 3 or more of the parameters our data suggest most strongly correlate to insulin secretion and plasma insulin (Basal Ca2+, 8G AD, 8G PD, 8G/QLA SD, 8G SD, 8G/QLA/GIP SD).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis.

claim: Many of the proteins correlated to Ca2+ parameters have been previously implicated in islet biology, including PCSK1, GCK, SUR1, GLUT2, PDX1, and GLP-1.
source: Interestingly, of the proteins correlated to these traits, many have been previously implicated in islet biology, including PCSK1, GCK, SUR1, GLUT2, PDX1, and GLP-1 (Whitticar and Nunemaker, 2020; Koneshamoorthy et al., 2022; Tengholm and Gylfe, 2017; Shuai et al., 2021; Koster et al., 2000; Remedi and Nichols, 2016; Jennings et al., 2020; Rutter et al., 2020; Stijnen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by cited references.

claim: The highly correlated proteins enriched for tissues, pathways, and transcription factors that support their role in insulin secretion.
source: Notably, the highly correlated proteins enriched for tissues, pathways, and transcription factors that support their role in insulin secretion (Figure 5B–D, Enrichr links in Supplementary file 3; Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a finding from the enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5B-D.

claim: Proteins highly anticorrelated to active duration in 8G were enriched for components of oxidative metabolism and had their gene promoters enrich for binding to the islet transcription factor MAFA.
source: For instance, proteins highly anticorrelated to active duration in 8G were enriched for components of oxidative metabolism and had their gene promoters enrich for binding to the islet transcription factor MAFA.
evidence: This is a finding from the enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5B-D.

claim: Human homologues were identified for 3073 proteins that were correlated to Ca2+ in either direction for at least one of the parameters of interest.
source: For each Ca2+ parameter, we focused on those proteins in the tails of the correlation histogram where r > |0.5| (e.g. Figure 5B). We identified human homologues for 3073 proteins that were correlated to Ca2+ in either direction for at least one of our parameters of interest.
evidence: This describes the data integration analysis.

claim: 647 human genes were strongly associated with diabetes-related SNPs.
source: We then searched the Type 2 Diabetes Knowledge Portal (https://t2d.hugeamp.org/) for SNPs that are associated with one or more glycemia-related traits (see Table 2) with a p-value <10–8, and are located within ±100 kbp of the homologous gene (e.g. COBLL1, Figure 6A), or in regions that contact the gene's promoter region (determined using human islet promoter-capture HiC data; Miguel-Escalada et al., 2019) as illustrated by ACP1 (Figure 6B). This yielded a list of 647 human genes strongly associated with diabetes-related SNPs.
evidence: This is a finding from the GWAS integration analysis shown in Figure 6.
